subject.title: Session transcript doomloop: crash-restart cycle inflates transcript until gateway OOMs

question: What default recovery policy should OpenClaw use when an active session transcript is too large or repeatedly re-bootstraps during gateway restart?
rationale: The code defect is clear, but the permanent behavior determines whether OpenClaw quarantines, truncates, skips, resets, or deduplicates user session state during recovery, which is a user-data and upgrade-policy decision.

options.title: Default Quarantine With Doctor Recovery
options.body: Detect oversized or repeated-bootstrap active transcripts before full open, skip the risky session during gateway startup, and surface a doctor or session command to inspect, compact, reset, or restore it.

options.title: Automatic Tail Truncation
options.body: Trim the oldest transcript content to a safe byte or line window during recovery, prioritizing availability but accepting automatic history loss.

options.title: Land Bootstrap Guard Only
options.body: Accept the current partial PR as a stopgap while leaving oversized transcript loading and media duplication to later work.

recommendation.title: Default Quarantine With Doctor Recovery
recommendation.body: Detect oversized or repeated-bootstrap active transcripts before full open, skip the risky session during gateway startup, and surface a doctor or session command to inspect, compact, reset, or restore it.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current code-history owner on the affected active-attempt, repair, session-manager, and bootstrap paths.
